description: Endoscopy room time per colonoscopy including turnover (T_P for case B)
source: Almeida R et al. 2016, Can J Gastroenterol Hepatol 2016:2574076, PMID 27446830 (in-room 52.9 min, turnover 7.9 min, 137 observations); Soderberg S et al. 2023, Health Serv Res Manag Epidemiol 10:23333928231159808, PMID 36923210 (in-room median 44.1-47.5 min, turnover mean 13.0 min, 177 colonoscopies); Day LW et al. 2014, Gastrointest Endosc 80:762-73, PMID 24796958 (procedure 28.5 min, turnover 13.2 min, US safety-net unit); Kidambi TD et al. 2024, Cureus 16:e69447, PMID 39411629 (wheels-in to wheels-out 26.5 min plus turnover 16.6 min, mixed procedures); corroborated by Frissora CL et al. 2025, One-Stop Colon and Endometrial Screening (ONCE), Proc (Bayl Univ Med Cent) 38(5):646-649, PMID 40821478, doi:10.1080/08998280.2025.2519596
notes: Base is a synthesis, not one study's value: in-room time plus turnover is about 57-61 min in Almeida and Soderberg and about 43 min in Kidambi (hospital ASC, about 60% colonoscopy). Low 40 and high 65 bracket those. Common scheduled slots are 30-60 min (Day 2014 modeled 45-60; Hubers 2020, PMID 31899692, reports a cut from 40 to 30). ONCE reports 54 min average total OR time (range 37-93) and 42 min procedure time for a combined EMB + colonoscopy (+ upper endoscopy when indicated) session; OR time is undefined and no component times are given, so it bounds colonoscopy alone from above and supports, but cannot narrow, 40-65.

description: OR time per laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy including turnover (T_P for case A)
source: Operative time: Clapp B et al. 2023, Surg Endosc 37:4113-22, PMID 36752855 (MBSAQIP 2015-2019, sleeve n=358,382, median 68 min). Non-operative in-room time: Sanford JA et al. 2015, Obes Surg 25:1078-85, PMID 25802066 (total OR minus operation time 55-72 min, RYGB); El Chaar M et al. 2023, Obes Surg 33:3411-21, PMID 37804468 (wheels-in to wheels-out minus operative time about 36 min). Turnover: Hoffman CR et al. 2018, BMC Med Educ 18:295, PMID 30518428 (mean 31 min). Cross-check: Kouzmina E et al. 2023, Obes Surg 33:2139-47, PMID 37199831 (sleeve anesthesia plus surgery 123-147 min, turnover 19-28 min)
notes: Base = 68 operative + 45 non-operative in-room + 30 turnover (synthesis of the sources). Low = 58 + 35 + 20; high = 78 + 60 + 40 (rounded). Laparoscopic; robotic sleeve runs about 20 min longer (Rahimi-Ardabily 2026 PMID 41116056).

description: OR time per laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass including turnover (T_P for the bypass variant)
source: Operative time: Clapp B et al. 2023, PMID 36752855 (MBSAQIP, RYGB n=123,357, median 113 min); Inaba CS et al. 2019, Surg Obes Relat Dis 15:1113-20, PMID 31128998 (BOLD, 104 min). In-room: Sanford JA et al. 2015, PMID 25802066 (total OR time 202-235 min by BMI group). Turnover: Hoffman CR et al. 2018, PMID 30518428
notes: Base = 113 operative + 45 non-operative + 30 turnover (rounded). High = Sanford's heaviest-BMI total OR time (235) + 30 turnover. Low = 104 + 35 + 20.

description: Added OR minutes to place an IUD under anesthesia at the end of bariatric surgery (dT for case A)
source: No published source found. Closest: O'Flynn O'Brien KL et al. 2019, J Pediatr Adolesc Gynecol 32:312-5, PMID 30633980 (office insertion speculum-in to speculum-out, median 383 s young adults, 555 s adolescents, n=95)
notes: PROVISIONAL (modeler judgment). About 5 min for the insertion plus 5-15 min to move a supine or split-leg bariatric patient into lithotomy, prep, and return. Use 3-5 min if the patient is already in lithotomy. A search for IUD or LARC placement at the time of bariatric or other unrelated surgery found feasibility and safety series (Hillard 2012 PMID 22831901; Schwartz 2020 PMID 32719107) but no timing data. Clapp 2020 (PMID 32712783, MBSAQIP) reports that concomitant procedures at bariatric surgery lengthen operative time.

description: Incremental procedure time to add EMB during an already-scheduled colonoscopy (dT for case B)
source: Huang et al. 2011, Prospective Study of Combined Colon and Endometrial Cancer Screening in Women With Lynch Syndrome (PMC3014510); reused from emb_colonoscopy config/model_parameters.csv @ 471e067; corroborated by Frissora CL et al. 2025, One-Stop Colon and Endometrial Screening (ONCE), Proc (Bayl Univ Med Cent) 38(5):646-649, PMID 40821478, doi:10.1080/08998280.2025.2519596
notes: Median 5 min, range 1-12 min, n=42 (MD Anderson). Triangular(1, 5, 12) as in emb_colonoscopy. ONCE (n=20, propofol, EMB performed first) reports only that the EMB typically takes less than 10 minutes, consistent with this range; it gives no measured increment, so base and range are unchanged.

description: Length of an OR block day for the integer-capacity model (B for case A)
source: Pandit JJ, Dexter F. 2009, Anesth Analg 108:1910-5, PMID 19448221 (OR sessions usually 8 h; models 8 vs 10 h staffing)
notes: Low = half-day (4 h) block; high = 10 h block. Used only in the integer-capacity day model (the expected-value net value does not depend on block length).

description: Length of an endoscopy room day for the integer-capacity model (B for case B)
source: Dexter F, Epstein RH, Penning DH. 2020, J Clin Anesth 59:18-25, PMID 31195226 (GI suite with 8-h allocated workdays); Day LW et al. 2014, PMID 24796958 (full days 8 AM-4 PM, half days 8 AM-12 PM)
notes: Low = half day; high = 10 h. Integer-capacity model only.

description: Probability u that the added OR minutes displace otherwise productive OR time (they would otherwise have held another bariatric case)
source: No direct source. Context: Dexter F et al. 1995, Anesth Analg 81:1263-8, PMID 7486114 (saving anesthesia-controlled minutes rarely permits one more case in an 8-h day); Dexter F et al. 2003, Anesth Analg 97:1119-26, PMID 14500168 (shorter turnover saves staffing cost rather than adding cases); Alvarez R et al. 2019, Ann Surg 270:1103-9, PMID 29794842 (bariatric waits driven by insurance requirements, not OR capacity)
notes: PROVISIONAL (modeler judgment). u = 1 means a fully booked OR with a ready backlog; u = 0 means slack capacity. Bariatric demand is paced by insurance pre-approval, so OR minutes are unlikely to be the binding constraint; base 0.25. The integer-capacity model shows when a lost case actually occurs.

description: Probability u that the added endoscopy minutes displace otherwise productive room time (they would otherwise have held another colonoscopy)
source: No direct source. Context: Hubers J et al. 2020, Clin Transl Gastroenterol 11:e00113, PMID 31899692 (screening/surveillance wait rose from 79 to 141 days); Shim HG et al. 2024, Clin Transl Gastroenterol 15:e1, PMID 38916225 (median wait 62.5-90.5 days); Joseph DA et al. 2016, Cancer 122:2479-86, PMID 27200481 (national colonoscopy capacity exceeds volume); Li X et al. 2026, J Med Syst 50, PMID 42337220 (unit throughput 53% of target, mainly room closures and delays)
notes: PROVISIONAL (modeler judgment). Colonoscopy backlogs are real in many systems, but national capacity exceeds use and unit throughput is limited more by staffing and delays than by a few minutes per case. Base 0.5 with a wide range.

description: Contribution margin (revenue minus variable cost) as a share of the primary payment for bariatric surgery (m for case A)
source: Mou D et al. 2023, Surg Endosc 37:6558-64, PMID 37308762 (Emory, 739 sleeve gastrectomies, cost accounting: revenue $19,134 vs variable cost $9,457 pre-COVID and $20,983 vs $11,235 post-COVID, margin 50.6% and 46.5%); Eappen S et al. 2013, JAMA 309:1599-606, PMID 23592104 (inpatient surgery without complications, margin share private 62.6%, Medicare 12.7%, Medicaid -22.0%)
notes: Base = midpoint of Mou's two periods (all payers, one academic center; abstract only). Low and high = Eappen's Medicare and private shares (all inpatient surgery, 2010, one system). Medicaid margins can be negative (Eappen); the model applies one share to each payer's own rate, so low-rate payers already yield small margins. Margin share depends heavily on how labor is classified (Roberts 1999 PMID 10029127: 16% of hospital cost variable).

description: Contribution margin as a share of the primary payment for hospital outpatient colonoscopy (m for case B)
source: No published per-case U.S. contribution margin found. Context: Henry SG et al. 2007, J Gen Intern Med 22:1415-21, PMID 17665271 (micro-costed direct cost $379 in 2001-2002 dollars, about $788 in 2026 medical-care CPI dollars); CMS OPPS Addendum B July 2026 (45378, APC 5311, $950.10); RAND 2024 (Whaley et al., private plans paid 289% of Medicare for outpatient hospital services, 2022 data); Roberts RR et al. 1999, JAMA 281:644-9, PMID 10029127
notes: PROVISIONAL (derived). Henry's inflated direct cost against the Medicare OPPS rate implies a margin share of about 0.17; against a commercial rate at 289% of Medicare about 0.71. Base 0.5 with low 0.2 and high 0.8.
